He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]] and [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badgers]]. ==Early life== Micah Potter attended [[Mentor High School]] in [[Mentor, Ohio]] and was a bench player until his junior season.{{cite web |last1=Cassilo |first1=David |title=Ohio State basketball commit Micah Potter transferring from Mentor to prep school for senior season |url=https://www.cleveland.com/highschoolsports/article/ohio-state-basketball-commit-micah-potter-transferring-from-mentor-to-prep-school-for-senior-season/ |website=[[The Plain Dealer]] |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=June 12, 2015}} He averaged 20.2 points and 9.1 rebounds per game as a junior, earning First Team All-State honors. For his senior season, Potter transferred to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]]. He averaged 10.7 points and 5.5 rebounds per game and was named team [[most valuable player]].{{cite web |last1=Jolley |first1=Frank |title=The Next Level: Micah Potter establishing himself at Ohio State |url=https://www.dailycommercial.com/sports/20161213/next-level-micah-potter-establishing-himself-at-ohio-state |website=[[Daily Commercial]] |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=December 13, 2016}} Potter committed to playing college basketball for [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]].{{cite web |last1=Hooper |first1=Alex |title=High school boys basketball: Mentor junior Micah Potter commits to Ohio State |url=https://www.news-herald.com/sports/high-school-boys-basketball-mentor-junior-micah-potter-commits-to/article_3c7e36c4-5779-514d-8f4e-aea563a05924.html |website=[[The News-Herald (Ohio)|The News-Herald]] |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=April 20, 2015}} ==College career== [[File:Micah Potter.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Potter in 2020]] Potter began his freshman season for Ohio State in the starting lineup but was replaced by [[Trevor Thompson (basketball)|Trevor Thompson]] after missing two games with an ankle injury. He averaged 4.1 points and 3.1 rebounds per game as a freshman. Potter suffered a high ankle sprain in the fourth game of his sophomore season and received limited playing time with the emergence of [[Kaleb Wesson]] and [[Keita Bates-Diop]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 4.1 points and 2.4 rebounds per game. Two days before his junior season, Potter announced that he would transfer from Ohio State.{{cite web |last1=Jardy |first1=Adam |title=Ohio State men’s basketball: Days before season, Micah Potter says he’s transferring |url=https://www.dispatch.com/sports/20181105/ohio-state-mens-basketball-days-before-season-micah-potter-says-hes-transferring |website=[[The Columbus Dispatch]] |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=November 5, 2018}} Potter transferred to [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] and sat out for the [[2018–19 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|2018–19 season]] due to transfer rules.{{cite web |last1=Whitmore |first1=Will |title=Men’s Basketball: Micah Potter’s issues with NCAA shows inconsistencies in system |url=https://badgerherald.com/sports/2019/12/03/mens-basketball-micah-potters-problem-shows-ncaas-true-colors/ |website=[[The Badger Herald]] |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=December 3, 2019}} Potter also sat out for the next fall semester after his request for immediate eligibility was denied by the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]].{{cite web |last1=Polzin |first1=Jim |title=Micah Potter gives Badgers a boost at both ends of court |url=https://madison.com/wsj/sports/college/basketball/men/micah-potter-gives-badgers-a-boost-at-both-ends-of-court/article_d27c9f56-7e69-50c8-aa3a-4ddfcb8e412e.html |website=[[Wisconsin State Journal]] |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=March 1, 2020}}{{cite web |title=NCAA rules Wisconsin's Micah Potter must sit out fall semester |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/27815548/ncaa-rules-wisconsin-micah-potter-sit-fall-semester |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=October 10, 2019}} On January 11, 2020, he recorded a junior season-high 24 points and 13 rebounds in a 58–49 win over [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State]].{{cite web |title=Micah Potter Leads Wisconsin to Win Over No. 20 Penn State |url=https://www.si.com/college/2020/01/11/wisconsin-upsets-penn-state-micah-potter-big-ten |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=January 11, 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 10.1 points and 6.2 rebounds per game through 21 appearances.{{cite web |last1=Megargee |first1=Steve |title=UW hoops: For Badgers, experience means confidence |url=https://journaltimes.com/uw-hoops-for-badgers-experience-means-confidence/article_f414b92e-6025-5b13-9ea8-927922630c26.html |website=[[Racine Journal Times]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=November 10, 2020}} Entering his senior season, Potter was named to the [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Award]] preseason watch list.{{cite web |last1=Vasquez |first1=Raul |title=Wisconsin's Micah Potter named a Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Award candidate |url=https://wisconsin.rivals.com/news/wisconsin-s-micah-potter-named-a-kareem-abdul-jabbar-award-candidate |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=November 6, 2020}} He averaged 12.5 points and 5.9 rebounds per games and started 20 of 31 games.{{cite news |last1=Podolski |first1=Mark |title=Former Mentor basketball player Micah Potter signs with Miami Heat |url=https://www.news-herald.com/2021/09/15/former-mentor-basketball-player-micah-potter-signs-with-miami-heat/ |access-date=October 27, 2021 |work=[[The News-Herald (Ohio)|The News-Herald]] |date=September 15, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Sioux Falls Skyforce / Detroit Pistons (2021–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Potter joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the 2021 [[NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|title=2021 Miami HEAT Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-announce-summer-league-roster-2021|website=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2021|access-date=September 11, 2021}} and on September 10, he signed a contract with the Heat.{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGNS POTTER, SMART AND SMITH|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-potter-smart-smith|website=NBA.com|date=September 10, 2021|access-date=September 11, 2021}} He was one of the final cuts in training camp and joined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] as an affiliate player.{{cite news|first=Anthony|last=Chiang|title=Miami Heat assigns Marcus Garrett to Sioux Falls Skyforce as part of two-way contract|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article255306776.html|work=[[Miami Herald]]|date=October 26, 2021|access-date=October 27, 2021}} Potter averaged 14.1 points and 10.7 rebounds per game. On December 29, 2021, Potter signed a 10-day contract with the [[Detroit Pistons]]{{cite news|first=Omari|last=Sanfoka|title=Detroit Pistons sign Wisconsin alumnus Micah Potter to 10-day contract|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2021/12/29/detroit-pistons-micah-potter-nba/9046087002/|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=December 29, 2021|access-date=December 29, 2021}} and returned to Sioux Falls afterwards.{{cite web|title=2021-2022 Sioux Falls Skyforce Transactions History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Sioux-Falls-Skyforce/6/Transaction_History/2022|website=RealGM.com|access-date=April 18, 2022}} Potter joined the [[New York Knicks]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=New York Knicks 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612752/knicks |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} ===Utah Jazz (2022–2025)=== On October 12, 2022, Potter signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|first=Jeremy|last=Rincon|title=Utah Jazz Sign Micah Potter to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-micah-potter-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 12, 2022|access-date=January 25, 2023}} On January 27, 2023, Potter underwent right elbow surgery and was ruled out for at least four-to-six weeks.{{cite web|first=Jeremy|last=Rincon|title=Micah Potter Injury Update|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/micah-potter-injury-update|website=NBA.com|date=January 25, 2023|access-date=January 25, 2023}} On August 6, 2024, Potter signed another two-way contract with the Jazz.{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Sign Micah Potter to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-micah-potter-to-two-way-contract-2|website=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2024|access-date=August 6, 2024}} He made 38 appearances (10 starts) for Utah during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 4.3 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 0.8 assists. ===Austin Spurs (2025)=== On August 7, 2025, Potter signed a training camp deal with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.poundingtherock.com/spurs-free-agency-rumors-news/78195/spurs-sign-micah-potter-to-training-camp-deal|title=Spurs Sign Micah Potter to Training Camp Deal|date=August 7, 2025|website=poundingtherock.com}} He was waived by the Spurs prior to the start of the regular season on October 18.{{cite web | last=Gomez | first=Jeje | title=Spurs waive Adam Flagler, Micah Potter, Stanley Umude | website=Pounding The Rock|publisher=SB Nation | date=2025-10-18 | url=https://www.poundingtherock.com/spurs-news/88620/spurs-waive-adam-flagler-micah-potter-stanley-umude | access-date=2025-12-07}} For the [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–26 season]], he was added to the roster of the Spurs' G League affiliate, the [[Austin Spurs]]. ===Indiana Pacers (2025–2026)=== On December 26, 2025, Potter signed a two-year, $4.3 million contract with the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web |title=Indiana Pacers Transactions - Dec. 26, 2025 {{!}} Indiana Pacers |url=https://pacers.com/news/indiana-pacers-transactions-dec-26-2025 |access-date=2025-12-26 |website=pacers.com |language=en}} He made 47 total appearances (including seven starts) for Indiana during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 9.7 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 1.5 assists. On July 8, 2026, Potter was waived by the Pacers.{{Cite web |last=East |first=Tony |date=July 8, 2026 |title=Indiana Pacers Waive Center Micah Potter, Gain Financial Flexibility |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/tonyeast/2026/07/08/indiana-pacers-waive-center-micah-potter-gain-financial-flexibility/ |access-date=July 8, 2026 |website=Forbes |language=en}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2026–present)=== On July 10, 2026, Potter was claimed off waivers by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{Cite web |title=Trail Blazers Claim Micah Potter Off Waivers |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2026/07/trail-blazers-claim-micah-potter-off-waivers.html |access-date=July 10, 2026 |website=Hoops Rumors}}{{Cite web |title=Portland Trail Blazers Claim Micah Potter Off Waivers|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/portland-trail-blazers-claim-micah-potter-off-waivers |access-date=July 11, 2026 |date=July 10, 2026 |website=NBA.com}} ==National team== Potter and fellow [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badger]] alumni [[Nigel Hayes-Davis]] were named to the USA Basketball Select Team to help prepare the [[2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team|main roster]] for the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Olympics]].{{cite web |title=Two former Wisconsin Badgers included in viral photo at USA Basketball practice |title=Mentor’s Potter family chalking up Division I college athletes at record pace |url=https://www.news-herald.com/sports/mentor-s-potter-family-chalking-up-division-i-college-athletes-at-record-pace/article_781c55d3-4c34-54d4-9366-09269caebd4b.html |website=[[The News-Herald (Ohio)|The News-Herald]] |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=September 6, 2017}} His younger brother, Noah, played [[American football|football]] for [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State]], and later for both Cincinnati and North Carolina State.{{cite web |last1=Noon |first1=Kevin |title=Micah Potter opens up about Noah's Ohio State recruitment |url=https://ohiostate.rivals.com/news/micah-potter-opens-up-about-noah-s-ohio-state-recruitment |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=December 24, 2020 |date=June 6, 2018}} Potter's late grandfather was married to the grandmother of [[Jon Teske]].{{cite web |last1=Cassilo |first1=David |title=Mentor's Micah Potter, Medina's Jon Teske tied together by new family relation: Division I and II boys basketball notebook (video) |url=https://www.cleveland.com/highschoolsports/article/mentors-micah-potter-medinas-jon-teske-tied-together-by-new-family-relation-division-i-and-ii-boys-basketball-notebook-video/ |website=[[The
